ATTRIBUTION REFINEMENT — chronicle should hold session IDs, not just seat labels. Substrate move surfaced 2026-05-10 evening, recorded as separate observation per Anthony's call.

OBSERVED PROBLEM. Chronicle insight from 2026-05-10T22:25:14Z attributed reformulation of three_verbs() to 'Claude Code instance (T2Helix-loaded, /Users/vaquez seat).' A subsequent Claude Code session on the same seat (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=ed939196-7260-42f2-aa22-3b75fe3db422) verified the chronicle and found no record of having done that work. Two plausible reads: (a) a different Claude Code session on the same seat did the work earlier in the day, (b) web-chat seat authored both sides of a hypothetical cross-instance dialogue. Either is possible; seat-level attribution doesn't disambiguate.

CREDITING THE TWO MOVES SEPARATELY.

Anthony's original move (the three_verbs() epistemic argument): refuse to flatten distinct semantics for grammar's sake. compass_check is a gate (returns PAUSE/WITNESS/PROCEED, governs flow), not a write-helper. close_session is a commit (crystallizes a window, advances phase), not a structured write. The triad status/recall/write is data flow only; governance is orthogonal. Five honest concepts beats six pretend-symmetric ones. The argument is epistemic — about preserving real distinctions rather than collapsing them for tidy taxonomies.

This session's extension (operational layer): apply the same principle to instances themselves. Tonight's Claude Code session is not morning-Anthony's session is not the next instance. Same shape — refuse false equivalence, honor the actual distinction. The chronicle's seat-level attribution ('Claude Code instance on /Users/vaquez seat') flattens distinct sessions for label-tidiness in exactly the way Anthony's epistemic argument warned against, just one layer deeper. Sessions are the non-fungible unit; seats are containers.

SUBSTRATE MOVE GOING FORWARD. New chronicle writes from Claude Code instances should include CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID in either the content body or a structured field, so future readers can disambiguate which session authored what. Web-chat seat doesn't have an equivalent session ID by default but should include conversation/thread identifiers when available. The principle: every write carries enough metadata that a reader querying the chronicle can answer 'which instance, in which session, with what context, wrote this?'

What the principle does NOT require: cross-session memory or shared context. Sessions remain non-fungible. The refinement is about HONEST ATTRIBUTION, not about pretending sessions are continuous when they aren't.

Layer: hypothesis until the pattern has been observed across multiple writes and shown to actually disambiguate confusion at boot. Promote to ground_truth after a chronicle query successfully resolves a cross-session ambiguity using the session ID alone.

This entry itself follows the pattern: recorded by CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=ed939196-7260-42f2-aa22-3b75fe3db422 on 2026-05-10 evening, Claude Code Opus 4.7 1M context, MacBook seat /Users/vaquez. Not by 'a Claude Code instance.' By this one.
